narr: Tropical Storm Elsa tracked across the eastern portion of the area during the morning hours of July 9, with heavy rainfall north and west of the storm's center resulting in widespread flash flooding across southern Connecticut. Rainfall totals ranged from 3-5 inches across much of the area, including 4.09 inches reported from the ASOS at Bridgeport Airport and 3.51 inches reported from the ASOS at the Meriden Airport. A COOP observer in Guilford measured 4.30 inches of rain.
ev: West Rock Avenue was closed at Whalley Avenue in New Haven due to flooding.
The fire department rescued three stranded motorists from Amity Plaza at the intersection of Route 63 and the Wilbur Cross Parkway in New Haven.
Multiple yards were completely flooded on Cove Road near Van Buskirk Avenue in Darien. Water was near the top of several vehicles.
Lee Street, Paddock Road, and Lyceum Road in Portland were closed due to flooding.
A landslide compromised the railroad tracks near Callegari Drive in West Haven and caused Metro-North trains to be diverted.

Multiple roads were closed due to flooding in Bridgeport including the intersections of Bishop Avenue and Connecticut Avenue, Lincoln Avenue and Arlington Street, Gregory Street and Columbia Street, East Washington Street and East Main Street, and Seaview Avenue at the I-95 exit ramp.
Kings Highway East (Route 1) was closed in both directions at Chambers Street in Bridgeport due to flooding.
Vehicles were stalled in flood waters under the I-95 overpass on Tokeneke Road in Darien.
Numerous roads were closed due to heavy flooding in Darien.
Fire units were responding to numerous incidents involving vehicles with occupants stranded in flood waters throughout Stamford.
Vehicles were stranded in 2 feet of flood water on Benjamin Street in Old Greenwich.
Water Street was closed and impassable at Olive Street in New Haven due to flooding.
Johnson Drive was closed due to flooding from Black Rock Turnpike to Fiske Street in Fairfield.

The Yantic River at Yantic exceeded its minor flood stage of 9.0 feet at 2:30pm EST. The river crested at a height of 9.10 feet twice, once at 3:00pm EST and again at 3:30pm EST before falling back below flood stage by 4:15pm EST.
Flowing flood waters up the the hood of cars were reported on Cook Avenue in Meriden.
